1.q: בִּ⁠שְׁנַת֙ שְׁבַֽע־עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה לְ⁠פֶ֖קַח בֶּן־רְמַלְיָ֑הוּ מָלַ֛ךְ אָחָ֥ז בֶּן־יוֹתָ֖ם מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה
1.note: In this verse and the next two verses, the author is introducing **Ahaz** as a participant in the story as the new king of **Judah**. To translate this verse, see how you translated the similar expressions in 8:16.

2.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 8:17. Alternate translation: [Ahaz was 20 years old]
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:2. Alternate translation: [But he did not do what Yahweh his God considered to be right]
See how you translated the similar expression in 8:24. Alternate translation: [his ancestor]

3.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 8:18. Alternate translation: [And he lived as the kings of Israel had lived]

The author is using **made … pass through the fire** as a common expression of his culture to mean “burned completely as an offering to an idol.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. The UST models one way to do that.
It might seem that this expression contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can shorten it. Alternate translation: [that Yahweh had driven out]

Here the phrase **from the face of** could: (1) be a common expression of the culture that means “on account of” or “on behalf of” a group. Alternate translation: [on behalf of the sons of Israel] or (2) represent [from the presence] of a group. Alternate translation: [from before the sons of Israel]
See how you translated the similar expression in 8:12. Alternate translation: [the Israelites]

4.note: The author is saying **every** green tree as a generalization for emphasis. If it would be clearer in your language, you could express the emphasis in a different way. Alternate translation: [and under green trees throughout his kingdom]

5.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 1:3. Alternate translation: [Then Rezin, the king of Aram, came]

The author assumes that readers will understand that by **fight**, in this context he means that the two kings were not immediately able to “overcome” or “defeat” Ahaz. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [but they were not able to defeat him right away]

6.q: בָּ⁠עֵ֣ת הַ⁠הִ֗יא הֵ֠שִׁיב רְצִ֨ין מֶֽלֶךְ־אֲרָ֤ם אֶת־אֵילַת֙ לַֽ⁠אֲרָ֔ם וַ⁠יְנַשֵּׁ֥ל אֶת־הַ⁠יְהוּדִ֖ים מֵֽ⁠אֵיל֑וֹת ו⁠ארמים בָּ֣אוּ אֵילַ֔ת וַ⁠יֵּ֣שְׁבוּ שָׁ֔ם עַ֖ד הַ⁠יּ֥וֹם הַ⁠זֶּֽה
6.note: The author is providing background information about something that Rezin did on this same military campaign. The author related in 14:22 how Azariah, the grandfather of Ahaz, recaptured Elath and brought it back under the control of the kingdom of Judah. The renewed loss of this city shows how the kingdom declined because of the idolatry of Ahaz. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.

6.q: הֵ֠שִׁיב & אֶת־אֵילַת֙ לַֽ⁠אֲרָ֔ם וַ⁠יְנַשֵּׁ֥ל אֶת־הַ⁠יְהוּדִ֖ים מֵֽ⁠אֵיל֑וֹת
6.note: The author is describing one event before describing another event that preceded it. If it would be helpful your language, you may wish to relate these events in the order in which they happened. Alternate translation: [drove the Judeans from Elath and restored Elath to Aram]
See how you translated the same expression in 2:22. Alternate translation: [and they are still living there at the time of this writing]

7.note: Ahaz is using each of the terms **servant** and **son** to offer to become a vassal of Tiglath-Pileser if he will help him. The term **servant** indicates more literally that Ahaz will obey Tiglath-Pileser, while the term **son** is a respectful form of address that makes Tiglath-Pileser, by implication, a “father” to Ahaz. See how you translated the term “son” in 8:9 and use a comparable expression for addressing someone respectfully in your language. You could also use plain language. Alternate translation: [I will obey you and I will be personally loyal to you]

In this context, the word **palm** represents power, as the word “hand” often does elsewhere in the book. Alternate translation: [from the power of the king of Aram and from the power of the king of Israel]

Ahaz is speaking as if Rezin and Pekah had actually **arisen** or stood up. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the ones who are attacking me]

8.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 12:18. Alternate translation: [the silver and the gold that was]
See how you translated the similar expression in 5:18. Alternate translation: [in the temple of Yahweh]

9.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 10:6. Alternate translation: [And the king of Assyria did what he asked]
Since the author has already used the title **the king of Assyria** earlier in this sentence, it may be more natural in your language to use a pronoun here. Alternate translation: [and he came up]
See how you translated the similar expression in 15:29. Alternate translation: [And he exiled the people of the city]

10.note: It might seem that this expression contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you can say this in a way that would be more natural. Alternate translation: [and the pattern for all of its work]

12.note: Since the author has already used the title **the king** earlier in this sentence, it may be more natural in your language to use a pronoun here. Alternate translation: [and he saw]

13.q: וַ⁠יַּקְטֵ֤ר אֶת־עֹֽלָת⁠וֹ֙ וְ⁠אֶת־מִנְחָת֔⁠וֹ וַ⁠יַּסֵּ֖ךְ אֶת־נִסְכּ֑⁠וֹ וַ⁠יִּזְרֹ֛ק אֶת־דַּֽם־הַ⁠שְּׁלָמִ֥ים אֲשֶׁר־ל֖⁠וֹ עַל־הַ⁠מִּזְבֵּֽחַ
13.note: To show that Ahaz not only **sprinkled … blood** on the **altar** but also did the other actions there, you may want to put the information that he did these things **on the altar** at the start of the verse. Alternate translation: [And on the altar he burned his burnt offering and his grain offering and poured out his drink offering and sprinkled the blood of the peace offerings that were to him]

14.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 3:14. Alternate translation: [was in the presence of Yahweh]
See how you translated the similar expression in 4:12. Alternate translation: [from in front of the temple]

The author assumes that readers will understand that when he says the bronze altar was **to the north** of the new altar, he means that it was on the right side of that altar. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [on the right]

15.note: The implication is that the new altar was larger than the old bronze altar. You could indicate in your translation that Ahaz is referring to the new altar here if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the new altar]

In this verse, the terms **burnt offering** and **sacrifice** are singular in form, but Ahaz is using them to describe every burnt offering and fellowship offering that would be offered on this altar. You could indicate this in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the blood of every burnt offering and the blood of every fellowship offering]

Ahaz is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [to seek guidance from Yahweh]

17.q: וַ⁠יְקַצֵּץ֩ הַ⁠מֶּ֨לֶךְ אָחָ֜ז אֶת־הַ⁠מִּסְגְּר֣וֹת הַ⁠מְּכֹנ֗וֹת וַ⁠יָּ֤סַר מֵֽ⁠עֲלֵי⁠הֶם֙ אֶת־הַ⁠כִּיֹּ֔ר וְ⁠אֶת־הַ⁠יָּ֣ם הוֹרִ֔ד מֵ⁠עַ֛ל הַ⁠בָּקָ֥ר הַ⁠נְּחֹ֖שֶׁת אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּחְתֶּ֑י⁠הָ וַ⁠יִּתֵּ֣ן אֹת֔⁠וֹ עַ֖ל מַרְצֶ֥פֶת אֲבָנִֽים׃ וְ⁠אֶת־מוּסַ֨ךְ הַ⁠שַּׁבָּ֜ת אֲשֶׁר־בָּנ֣וּ בַ⁠בַּ֗יִת וְ⁠אֶת־מְב֤וֹא הַ⁠מֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ הַֽ⁠חִיצ֔וֹנָ⁠ה הֵסֵ֖ב בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה מִ⁠פְּנֵ֖י מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר
17.note: Ahaz took all of the actions that the author describes in 16:17 and 16:18 **from the face of the king of Assyria**, that is, out of deference to him or to please him. If it would be helpful to your readers, in order to indicate this, you could combine these two verses into a verse bridge. You could put the phrase **from the face of the king of Assyria**, which gives the reason for Ahaz’s actions, at the beginning. Alternate translation: [And from the face of the king of Assyria, King Ahaz cut off the panels of the stands, and he removed the basin from upon them, and he took down the sea from upon the oxen of bronze that were beneath it and put it on a pavement of stones, and the canopy of the Sabbath that they had built at the house and the outer entrance of the king, he removed from the house of Yahweh]
These are all technical terms relating to the furnishings of the temple courtyard. If you have already translated the book of 1 Kings, see how you translated these terms in 1 Kings 7:23–39.

In this verse, the word **basin** is singular in form, but it refers to the basins on all ten of the **stands** in the temple courtyard. You could indicate this in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the basins from upon them] or [the basin that was on each one]

18.note: Here the author is using the pronoun **they** in a general sense, not to refer to specific people. Use an expression for this that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [that had been built]
See how you translated the similar expression in 16:3. Alternate translation: [on account of]

19.q: וְ⁠יֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י אָחָ֖ז אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲ⁠לֹא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַ⁠יָּמִ֖ים לְ⁠מַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה
19.note: In this verse and the next verse, the author is concluding the story of Ahaz. To translate this verse, see how you translated the similar phrases in 1:18.

20.note: See how you translated the same expression in 8:24. Alternate translation: [And Ahaz passed away] or [And Ahaz died]

The expression **was buried** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and people buried him in the same place where people had buried his ancestors]
